mainTopic: Items a woman may not wear out on שבת, and the טבילה-based reason for banning hair-strings
overview: This amud opens a new perek with a משנה about which items a woman may wear when she goes out into רשות הרבים on שבת. The משנה forbids hair-strings of wool or flax, several head ornaments, and a group of jewelry. It says that going out with them by mistake does not require a חטאת, because these are real ornaments and the ban is only a rabbinic גזירה. The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions טבילה. רבה בר אבוה explains that the טבילה line gives the reason for the ban: she must loosen the strings to immerse, so on שבת she might untie them and carry them four אמות. רב then rules that woven chains were never included in the גזירה. Two versions of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's support follow, and the גמרא shows that they differ about dirty chains. Next the גמרא quotes a משנה from מקוואות about strings that are a חציצה, and רב הונא limits it to strings tied in the hair. רב יוסף explains that neck strings are excluded because a woman does not choke herself. אביי challenges this from a ברייתא that forbids neck straps, and רבינא begins to answer at the end of the amud.

steps.title: The opening heading of the perek
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with a framing question: with what may a woman go out on שבת, and with what may she not?
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With what may a woman go out on שבת, and with what may she not go out?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up the topic of the whole perek with a heading question. The list of actual rulings comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying from one domain to another on שבת is forbidden, but wearing clothing or jewelry is not considered carrying. This perek sorts out which worn items count as normal clothing or ornaments and which are a problem. The question format just organizes the list. It is not a real challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Goes out (into the public domain on שבת)

phrases.english: MISHNA: With what may a woman go out,
phrases.notes: "Go out" means into רשות הרבים on שבת while wearing the item.

phrases.english: and with what may she not go out?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמָּה אִשָּׁה יוֹצְאָה, וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek (parallels the previous perek's opening about animals).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the topic: sorting permitted and forbidden items a woman wears out on שבת.

steps.title: No going out with wool, flax, or other strips braided into the hair
steps.stepSummary: A woman may not go out on שבת with strings of wool or flax, or strips of other material, tied into her hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may not go out with strings of wool, nor with strings of flax, nor with strips that are in her head.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first forbidden item: hair-ties made of wool, flax, or other strips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These hair-ties are ordinary ornaments. They are not a burden. The concern, as the גמרא will explain, is that she may need to remove them for טבילה and then carry them four אמות in רשות הרבים. So the ban is a protective rabbinic גזירה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these items are forbidden because they are a 'burden' (משאוי). They are real ornaments. The ban is only a precaution against her taking them off and carrying them.

phrases.english: A woman may not go out
neither with strings of wool
nor with strings of flax
nor with strips that are in her head.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תֵּצֵא אִשָּׁה לֹא בְּחוּטֵי צֶמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the heading question with the first forbidden items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hair-ties of wool, flax, or other strips may not be worn out into רשות הרבים on שבת.

steps.title: Side rule: hair-ties must be loosened before immersion
steps.stepSummary: A woman may not do טבילה with these strings in her hair until she loosens them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she may not immerse with them until she loosens them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a side ruling about the same hair-ties, this time about immersing in a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tight strings block the water from reaching her hair. That makes them a חציצה (barrier), and a barrier invalidates the טבילה. Once she loosens them, the water can reach her hair, and the טבילה is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrier blocking water from the body during טבילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This side rule is the key to the שבת ban in step 2. Since she must remove or loosen the ties for טבילה, she might take them off and carry them on שבת.

phrases.english: And she may not immerse with them until she loosens them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a non-שבת ruling about the same items from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tight hair-ties are a חציצה, so they must be loosened before טבילה.

steps.title: Forehead ornaments and head coverings
steps.stepSummary: A woman may not go out with a טוטפת. She may not go out with סרביטין unless they are sewn on. She may not go out with a כבול into רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with a טוטפת, and not with סרביטין when they are not sewn, and not with a כבול into the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the forbidden list with ornaments and coverings worn on the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טוטפת is a band worn across the forehead. The סרביטין are hanging ornaments that are forbidden only when they are not sewn to her head covering. If they are sewn on, they cannot fall off or be removed and carried. The כבול (a cap or hairnet) is forbidden specifically into רשות הרבים, which suggests it is allowed in a courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: A cap or hairnet worn on the head

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'into רשות הרבים' are attached here to the כבול. The גמרא later discusses whether that limit applies only to the כבול or to other items too, so do not assume yet.

phrases.english: and not with a totefet,
and not with sarvitin at a time when they are not sewn.
phrases.notes: If they are sewn to the head covering, they are permitted.

phrases.english: and not with a kavul into the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden items, moving to forehead and head ornaments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not go out with a טוטפת, with unsewn סרביטין, or with a כבול into רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Forbidden jewelry: city of gold, necklace, nose rings, ring, needle
steps.stepSummary: A woman may not go out with an עיר של זהב, a קטלא, nose rings, a ring without a seal, or a needle without a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with a city of gold, and not with a קטלא, and not with nose rings, and not with a ring that has no seal on it, and not with a needle that is not perforated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes this part of the list with a group of women's jewelry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עיר של זהב is a gold ornament engraved with an image of ירושלים. The קטלא is a necklace. Nose rings, a ring without a seal, and a needle without a hole are all purely decorative women's items. They are real תכשיטין. The concern is that she may take one off to show a friend and then carry it in רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: A gold ornament shaped like (engraved with) ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: Every item in this list is forbidden even though it is a genuine ornament. The rabbinic concern is that she might remove it and carry it in רשות הרבים. A ring without a seal and a needle without a hole are singled out because they are purely decorative women's jewelry.

phrases.english: and not with a city of gold,
and not with a katla, and not with nose rings,
and not with a ring that has no seal on it,
and not with a needle that is not perforated.
phrases.notes: A decorative pin, not a sewing tool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of forbidden items here with jewelry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not go out on שבת with an עיר של זהב, a קטלא, nose rings, a ring without a seal, or a needle without a hole.

steps.title: No sin-offering if she went out with these items
steps.stepSummary: If a woman went out with any of the items listed, she does not have to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she went out with them, she is not obligated to bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list by saying that a woman who went out with these items does not bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought for breaking a Torah-level איסור by mistake. These items count as jewelry, and the Torah allows a woman to wear jewelry outside. The ban is only a rabbinic גזירה, made in case she takes an item off and carries it, so there is no חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering brought for accidentally breaking a Torah prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: Everything in this משנה is forbidden only by the חכמים, not by the Torah. That is why going out with these items by mistake does not require a חטאת.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'not liable' as 'allowed.' She is still not supposed to go out with these items. The point is only that she does not bring a חטאת.

phrases.english: And if she went out (with them)
she is not obligated to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה's list of forbidden items by stating what happens if she went out with them anyway
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out with these items is only a rabbinic איסור, so there is no חטאת.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention immersion at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why a משנה about שבת brings up the laws of טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Immersion — who mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out that the line about טבילה seems out of place in a משנה about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about what a woman may wear outside on שבת. A rule about immersing with strings in her hair seems to belong to a different topic. The גמרא wants to know why it is here.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Who mentioned its name? (Why is this topic here at all?)

phrases.english: Gemara:
Immersion — who mentioned it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why Step 3, the line about טבילה, appears in a משנה about שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה is about שבת, so a rule about טבילה looks like it does not belong here.

steps.title: The immersion line explains the reason for the שבת rule
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה reads the טבילה line as the reason for the שבת ban. Since she must untie the strings for טבילה, she might untie them on שבת and carry them four אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The משנה is giving a reason. Why may a woman not go out with wool or flax strings? Because the חכמים said that even on a weekday she may not immerse with them until she loosens them. Since that is true, on שבת she may not go out with them. Otherwise, she might need to immerse for a מצוה, untie them, and end up carrying them four אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה answers that the טבילה line is not a separate topic. It is the reason behind the שבת rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strings tied tightly in the hair block the water, so she must loosen them before טבילה. If she goes out wearing them on שבת and needs a טבילה של מצוה, she might take them off. Then she might carry them four אמות in רשות הרבים, which is a real שבת איסור. So the חכמים banned wearing them outside at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is stating a reason (the משנה is explaining why)
An immersion she is required to do, such as after נדה
Four cubits, the distance at which carrying becomes a שבת איסור

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on hair strings is a גזירה built on a chain of worries: she must untie them for טבילה, so she might untie them on שבת, and then she might carry them in רשות הרבים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the test for the rest of the sugya. A hair item is forbidden if it would need to be removed for טבילה. That is exactly why the next steps ask about woven items.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
It (the Mishnah) is stating a reason:
What is the reason a woman may not go out

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּחוּטֵי צֶמֶר וְלֹא בְּחוּטֵי פִּשְׁתָּן —
phrases.english: with strings of wool or with strings of flax?
Because the Sages said

phrases.aramaic: בַּחוֹל לָא תִּטְבּוֹל בָּהֶן עַד שֶׁתְּרַפֵּם.
phrases.english: that on a weekday she may not immerse with them until she loosens them.
And since on a weekday she may not immerse with them
until she loosens them,
on Shabbat she may not go out (with them),

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא מִיתְרְמֵי לַהּ טְבִילָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה
phrases.english: lest a מצוה immersion happen to come up for her
and she untie them,
and come to carry them four cubits
in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 by reading the טבילה line as the reason for the שבת rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: the second clause gives the reason for the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טבילה line looked like an unrelated law placed in a משנה about שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טבילה line explains the שבת ban. Since she must untie the strings for טבילה, she might untie them on שבת and carry them in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks about hollow woven chains
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks רב what the law is for hollow chains made of strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא asked רב: What is the law regarding hollow chains?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks whether a woman may wear hollow string chains in her hair on שבת. This sets up רב's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on Step 8, the question is whether these hollow chains block water like tied strings do. If they block water, she would have to remove them for טבילה, and the גזירה would apply.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana asked Rav:
Hollow chains — what (is the law)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason from Step 8 to a new type of hair item
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do hollow string chains fall under the גזירה on hair strings?

steps.title: Woven items were not included in the decree
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the חכמים made no גזירה on anything woven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You mean woven? Anything woven, they did not decree against.
steps.whatsHappening: רב replies that these chains are woven, and the חכמים did not include woven items in the גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woven chain is loose enough that water reaches the hair through it. So she does not need to remove it for טבילה. With no reason to take it off, there is no worry that she will carry it, and the גזירה does not apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גזירה follows its reason exactly. If an item does not need to be removed for טבילה, the חכמים did not forbid it.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are speaking of something woven?
Anything that is woven, they did not decree against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's question from Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Hollow chains are woven, and woven items were not included in the גזירה.

steps.title: Another אמורא says the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע also said that woven items were not included in the גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Anything woven, they did not decree against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב's ruling by quoting another אמורא who said the exact same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase איתמר נמי means 'it was also stated.' It brings a separate report that matches the ruling just given. This makes רב's rule about woven items stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a matching report)

steps.whatToRemember: Hair strings are forbidden outside on שבת because she might untie them for טבילה and carry them. Woven items let water through, so they were never included in the גזירה.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Anything that is woven, they did not decree against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling in Step 10 with a matching statement from another אמורא
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that woven items were not included in the גזירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A matching statement of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע

steps.title: Second version: רב הונא's sisters were not bothered by the chains
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's support: he saw that his sisters were not bothered by these chains, so the chains do not need to be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the statement went like this: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said, 'I saw that my sisters were not bothered by them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the support for רב's ruling. Here the support is not a general rule about woven items. It is something רב הונא saw women in his family do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thing on the body counts as a barrier for טבילה only if the person is bothered by it and would want it off. רב הונא's sisters left the chains on and did not care, so the chains are not a barrier. If she never needs to untie them for טבילה, there is no worry that she will untie them on שבת and carry them. So there is no reason for a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces a second version of a statement
They are particular, meaning bothered by something and wanting it removed

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree that hollow woven chains are allowed. They differ only in the REASON. That difference in reasoning sets up the next question.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
I saw my sisters
that they are not particular about them.
phrases.notes: They bathed with the chains still in their hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the support quoted in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that hollow chains of strings are permitted on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's report of his sisters' practice: they were not bothered by the chains

steps.title: What difference is there between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two versions of רב הונא's statement lead to any different result in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between this version and that version?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It asks whether the two versions give different practical results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Version one says the חכמים never made a גזירה on woven things. Version two says the chains are fine because women are not bothered by them. Both permit the chains, so the גמרא looks for a case where the two reasons would split.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between them?

phrases.english: What is there
between this version
and that version?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין הַךְ לִישָּׁנָא וּבֵין הַךְ לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the version in Step 12 with the version in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two versions give different practical results

steps.title: The difference: dirty chains
steps.stepSummary: The versions differ when the chains are dirty. Under the 'woven' version they are still permitted. Under the 'not bothered' version a woman is bothered by dirty chains, so they would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is dirty chains. The first version said the חכמים made no גזירה on anything woven, and these are also woven, so they are permitted. The second version said it depends on whether she is bothered by them. Since these are dirty, she certainly is bothered by them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two versions split in the case of dirty chains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'woven' version, dirt changes nothing: the chain is still woven, and woven items were left out of the גזירה. Under the 'bothered' version, a woman is bothered by a dirty chain and would take it off. That makes it a barrier (חציצה) she must remove for טבילה. So the old worry returns: she might untie it on שבת and carry it, and it would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Being bothered by something, which can make it a barrier for טבילה

steps.whatToRemember: Woven hollow chains are permitted. The two versions differ only for dirty chains. The 'woven' reason permits them, while the 'bothered' reason forbids them.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where they are dirty.
According to this version, which said:
anything woven, they did not decree upon —
these too are woven, so they are permitted;
and according to that version, where you said it depends on being bothered —
since it is dirty,
she is certainly bothered by them.
phrases.notes: So she would remove them for טבילה, and on שבת they would be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dirty woven chains: permitted under the 'woven' version, forbidden under the 'bothered' version.

steps.title: The משנה in מקוואות on strings that block water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מקוואות. Wool strings, linen strings, and girls' hair straps count as barriers (חציצה) for טבילה. רבי יהודה says wool and hair strings do not, because water gets through them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there in a משנה: These are barriers on a person: wool strings, linen strings, and the straps on girls' heads. רבי יהודה says: wool strings and hair strings are not barriers, because water gets through them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source from מסכת מקוואות about which strings block the water of טבילה. This sets up a clarification that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our שבת משנה links its ruling to טבילה, so the גמרא turns to the main source on what blocks water. The תנא קמא says wool and linen strings and hair straps are barriers. רבי יהודה disagrees about wool and hair, since water soaks through those materials and still reaches the body.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there: quotes a משנה from another מסכת
Act as a barrier between the body and the water of the מקוה
Flax, which is used to make linen

phrases.english: We learned there:
And these are barriers on a person:
strings of wool and strings of flax,
and the straps that are on girls' heads.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל צֶמֶר וְשֶׁל שֵׂעָר אֵין חוֹצְצִין
phrases.english: those of wool and those of hair are not barriers,
because the water comes through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the chains discussion to the core source on what counts as a barrier for טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא counts wool and linen strings and hair straps as barriers. רבי יהודה exempts wool and hair because water passes through them.

steps.title: רב הונא: the משנה is about strings tied in girls' hair
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא clarifies that every item in the משנה's list refers to strings tied in girls' hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: we learned all of these only about the strings on girls' heads.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא limits the משנה we just read. The list of barriers is about strings tied in the hair, not strings worn elsewhere on the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the משנה plainly, one might think wool or linen strings anywhere on the body are a barrier. רב הונא says the משנה's whole list is about hair ties, which are bound tightly into the hair. This narrows the case, so other placements need their own discussion.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not adding new items to the list. He is telling us WHERE all the listed strings are: in the hair of girls.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
And all of them, we learned regarding girls' heads.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְכוּלָּן, בְּרָאשֵׁי הַבָּנוֹת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of the משנה quoted in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the strings listed in the משנה as barriers refer to strings tied in girls' hair.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what רב הונא is excluding, starting with wool neck strings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what רב הונא's statement is meant to leave out. If it leaves out wool strings on the neck, that makes no sense. Wool on hair is already a barrier, so wool on soft neck skin should certainly be one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: What does רב הונא mean to exclude? Suppose you say neck strings. Then strings made of what? Suppose you say wool. But the משנה already says soft wool on top of hard hair is a barrier. Do we even need to say that soft wool on top of soft skin is a barrier?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב הונא's statement from Step 16. That statement implied that strings around the neck are not a barrier. רב יוסף starts testing this with wool strings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair counts as 'hard' and neck skin counts as 'soft.' A string sinks into soft skin more than into hair, so it blocks water even more. If wool on hair is already a חציצה, wool on the neck should be one all the more. So it cannot be that רב הונא meant to exclude wool neck strings.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it (a sharp challenge)
Something soft on top of something hard
Is it even necessary to say? (it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'hard' and 'soft' describe the body surface under the string, not only the string. Hair is the 'hard' surface. The neck's flesh is the 'soft' surface, and a string presses into it more.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objects to it:
To exclude what?
If you say, to exclude strings of the neck,
then strings of what material?
If you say, to exclude strings of wool —

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא רַךְ עַל גַּבֵּי קָשֶׁה חוֹצֵץ,
phrases.english: now, if soft wool on top of hard hair is a barrier,
is it even necessary to say that soft wool on soft neck skin is one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's statement in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that the משנה's list refers only to hair strings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A neck string presses into soft skin more than into hair. So if wool in the hair is a barrier, wool on the neck should be one even more. Excluding it makes no sense.

steps.title: Flax neck strings cannot be what רב הונא excludes either
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tries a second option: maybe רב הונא meant to exclude flax neck strings. The same problem comes back. Hard flax on hard hair is a barrier, so hard flax on soft neck skin should certainly be one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, then, he meant to exclude strings of flax. But the משנה already says hard flax on top of hard hair is a barrier. Do we even need to say that hard flax on top of soft skin is a barrier?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף continues his challenge. He tests the other material, flax, and shows that it fails the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flax is a stiff, 'hard' material. If flax on hair already blocks water, flax pressing into soft neck skin blocks it even more. With both wool and flax ruled out, the simple reading of רב הונא has nothing it could be excluding.

keyTerms.meaning: Something hard on top of something soft

phrases.english: Rather, perhaps it is to exclude strings of flax.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא קָשֶׁה עַל גַּבֵּי קָשֶׁה חוֹצֵץ,
phrases.english: Now, if hard flax on top of hard hair is a barrier,
phrases.notes: Some render this as 'wool'. In context the string meant is flax.

phrases.english: is it even necessary to say that hard flax on soft neck skin is one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge of Step 17 by ruling out the second material, flax
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that רב הונא excludes flax neck strings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'all the more so' logic: a neck string presses into soft skin even harder than into hair.

steps.title: רב יוסף's new reason: a woman does not choke herself
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains רב הונא differently. Neck strings are not a barrier because a woman never ties anything tightly around her neck. Water can always get underneath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: This is the reason of רב הונא. A woman does not choke herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף replaces the physical 'soft and hard' approach with a practical reason. This explains why neck strings are excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not the material or the body surface. It is how tightly the string is tied. Hair strings are tied tightly, but no woman ties a neck ornament so tightly that she chokes. So water reaches the skin, and there is no חציצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle about loose neck ornaments. אביי immediately tests this principle in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said,
this is the reason of Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אִשָּׁה חוֹנֶקֶת אֶת עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.english: because a woman does not choke herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty רב יוסף raised in Steps 17–18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's exclusion was about the material or the softness of the neck, which made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neck strings are excluded because they are always tied loosely. A woman does not choke herself.

steps.title: אביי challenges from the rule about girls' neck straps on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. Girls may go out on שבת with strings in their ears, but not with straps around their necks. If neck straps are always loose, why are they forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Girls may go out with strings in their ears, but not with straps around their necks. If you say a woman does not choke herself, why may they not go out with straps around their necks?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's new reason using a ברייתא about going out on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Girls may not go out on שבת wearing items they might take off for טבילה, because they may end up carrying them. If neck straps are always loose, they would not be a barrier and would not need to be removed. So the ban on neck straps suggests that they can be tight.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
Strings in their ears (to keep pierced holes open)

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
Girls may go out with strings in their ears,
but not with straps around their necks.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין אִשָּׁה חוֹנֶקֶת עַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say a woman does not choke herself,
why may they not go out with straps around their necks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reason given in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's principle that a woman does not choke herself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids neck straps on שבת. That only makes sense if they could be a barrier for טבילה, meaning they can be tied tightly. This goes against the principle.

steps.title: רבינא begins his response
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רבינא, who is about to address אביי's challenge from the ברייתא about neck straps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא names the next speaker, רבינא, who is about to respond to אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי just asked a question. If a woman never ties anything tightly around her neck, why does the ברייתא forbid girls from going out on שבת with neck straps? רבינא's words open the next move, which explains why straps are different. His actual explanation appears in the following text.

keyTerms.meaning: רבינא, a late אמורא in Babylonia

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for an answer in these two words alone. They only tell you who is speaking next. רבינא's actual explanation comes right after this.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
phrases.notes: Here רבינא starts his answer to אביי's challenge from step 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a response to אביי's challenge from the ברייתא, which forbids neck straps on שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduction of a responding sage. The resolution itself follows in the next text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If neck items are never tight, as רב יוסף said, then neck straps should not be forbidden.
